newsitem.title: USA: Texas power prices climb with higher natgas prices.
newsitem.headline: Texas power prices climb with higher natgas prices.

text.p: Bulk wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) climbed Monday with higher natural gas prices and despite the return of some Texas power generation, industry sources said.
"With gas prices as high as they are it doesn't much matter that we have a couple of more (power) units on line," said one Houston-based ERCOT marketer.

Peak, firm electricity in ERCOT for Tuesday delivery was said to be talked at $23.00-26.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from discussion near $23.00 for Monday delivery late last week, the brokers and marketers said.
The power prices moved higher despite the return of Texas Utilities' 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear power unit 2 over the weekend from a repair outage.
Also, Lower Colorado River Authority's 430 megawatt Ferguson natural gas-fired unit returned to service over the weekend.
ERCOT power prices were also said to have been strengthed by forecasts of below-normal weather through to the end of October, possibly making for some heating demand, the sources said.
Spot natural gas prices were said to have increased by about five cents per million British thermal units in Texas Monday.
Off-peak ERCOT power for Tuesday delivery was said to have held steady the $12.50-14.50 range, the sources said.
November ERCOT electricity was talked steady at $20.25-20.50, while December was assessed steady at $22.25-22.50 per MWh.
Also, South Texas Electric Cooperative planned to shut its 400 megawatt San Miguel coal-fired plant on October 21 for maintenance that was expected to last no more than five days.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
